question: During septoplasty for a severe caudal septal deviation, the surgeon must preserve the L-strut. Which of the following correctly describes the L-strut and the consequence of its violation?

answers.text: The L-strut is the posterior bony portion of the septum; its loss causes saddle-nose deformity.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The L-strut refers to the anterior and caudal cartilaginous support framework, not the posterior bony septum. It is the quadrilateral cartilage's anterior and inferior limbs.

answers.text: The L-strut is a 1 cm-wide strip of quadrilateral cartilage along the dorsum and caudal septum; removing too much results in saddle-nose deformity and columellar retraction.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The L-strut (dorsal strut 1 cm + caudal strut 1 cm) maintains the structural integrity of the external nose. Violation leads to saddle-nose deformity dorsally and columellar retraction or tip ptosis caudally.

answers.text: The L-strut is the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid; its resection causes cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhoea.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While the perpendicular plate of the ethmoid is part of the septum and its aggressive resection near the cribriform plate can risk CSF leak, it is not the L-strut. The L-strut is entirely cartilaginous.

answers.text: The L-strut is the vomerian component of the septum; its preservation is required to avoid palatal dehiscence.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The vomer forms the posteroinferior bony septum; it has no role in external nasal support. The L-strut is the cartilaginous support framework of the nasal dorsum and columella.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the anatomy section and the clinical pearl on L-strut preservation. This is a high-yield operative landmark.
Correct. Always preserve at least 1 cm of dorsal and caudal cartilage — the L-strut — to prevent post-septoplasty nasal collapse.
